πληρόω.sd: to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc.
πληρόω.kj: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply
πληρόω.as:
πληρόω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for מָלֵא;]
1.to fill, make full, fill to the full, c. acc.;
(a) of things: pass. (σαψήνη, φάραγξ), Mt 13:48, Lk 3:5(LXX); fig., Mt 23:32; but chiefly of immaterial things: πᾶσαν χρείαν, Phl 4:19; ἦχος ἐπλήρωσε τ. οἶκον, Ac 2:2; c. gen. rei (cl.), Ac 5:28; pass., seq. ἐκ, Jo 12:3 (cf. B1., § 36, 4); π. τ. καρδίαν, Jo 16:6, Ac 5:3; metaph., of the all-pervading activity of Christ, Eph 4:10; mid., Eph 1:23;
(b) of persons: to fill with, cause to abound in: c. gen. rei (cl.), Ac 2:28(LXX), Ro 15:13; pass., to be filled with, abound in: Eph 3:19, Phl 4:18; c. gen. rei (cl.), Ac 13:52, Ro 15:14, II Ti 1:4; c. dat. (Æsch., al.), Lk 2:40 (c. gen., T), Ro 1:29, II Co 7:4; c. acc. (so in π., v. MM, xx), Phl 1:11, Col 1:9; seq. ἐν, Eph 5:18, Col 2:10.
2.to complete;
(a)to complete, fulfil: of number, Re 6:11, WH, txt.; of time (MM, xx), Mk 1:15, Lk 21:24, Jo 7:8, Ac 7:23, 309:2324:27; ἐυδοκίαν, II Th 1:11; τ. χαράν, Phl 2:2; pass., Jo 3:2915:1116:2417:13, I Jo 1:4, II Jo 12; τ. ἔργα, Re 3:2; ἡ ὑπακοή, II Co 10:6; τ. πάσχα, Lk 22:16;
(b)to execute, accomplish, carry out to the full: Mt 3:15, Lk 7:19:31, Ac 12:2513:2514:2619:21, Ro 8:413:815:19, Ga 5:14, Col 1:254:17, Re 6:11, T, WH, R, mg.;
(c) of sayings, prophecies, etc., to bring to pass, fulfil: Mt 1:222:15, 17, 234:145:178:1712:1713:3521:426:54, 5627:9, Mk 14:4915:28 (WH, R, txt. om.), Lk 1:204:2124:44, Jo 12:3813:1815:2517:1218:9, 3219:24, 36, Ac 1:163:1813:27, Ja 2:23 (cf. Lft., Col., 255 ff.).†

πλοῖον.as:
πλοῖον, -ου, τό
(< πλέω), [in LXX chiefly for אֳנִיָּה;]
a boat, also (= obsol. ναῦς) a ship: Mt 4:21, 22, and freq. in Gosp. and Ac, Ja 3:4, Re 8:918:19.

πλησίον.sd: (adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend)

πλατύς.as:
πλατύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX for רָחָב;]
broad: Mt 7:13. As subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for רְחֹב;] a street: Mt 6:512:19(LXX), Mk 6:56, WH, mg., Lk 10:1013:2614:21, Ac 5:15, Re 11:821:2122:2.†

πλατεῖα.long: a street, public square, broad way.
πλατεῖα.sd: a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square

πλήρωμα.long: (a) a fill, fullness; full complement; supply, patch, supplement, (b) fullness, filling, fulfillment, completion.
πλήρωμα.sd: repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period)
πλήρωμα.kj: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness
πλήρωμα.as:
πλήρωμα, -τος, τό
(< πληρόω), [in LXX for מְלֹא;]
the result of the action involved in πληρόω (Lft., Col., 255 ff.; AR, Eph., 255 ff.), hence,
1. in passive sense, that which has been completed, complement, plenitude, fullness (in Xen., Luc., Polyb., al., of a ship's crew or cargo, and by meton. of the ship itself): Jo 1:16, Ro 11:12, 2515:29, I Co 10:26(LXX), Eph 1:23 (AR, 42 ff.) 3:19 (AR. 87 ff.) 4:13, Col 1:192:9; of time, Ga 4:4, Eph 1:10; κοφίνων (σφυρίδων) πληρώματα, basketfuls, Mk 6:438:20.
2. In active sense (= πλήρωσις, as freq. in words of these formations, cf. κτίσις, and v. MM, xx);
(a)that which fills up (but v. Lft., Col., 255 ff.): Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21;
(b)a filling up, completing, fulfilment: Ro 13:10.†

πλήν.long: however, nevertheless, but, except that, yet.
πλήν.sd: moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet
πλήν.kj: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than
πλήν.as:
πλήν,
adv.,
[in LXX for רַק, לְבַד, אַךְ, etc.;]
1. introducing a clause (= ἀλλά, δέ; "it is obvious that πλήν was the regular word in the vulgar language": Bl., § 77, 13), yet, howbeit, only: Mt 11:22, 2418:726:39, 64 (M, Pr., 86), Lk 6:24, 3510:11, 14, 2011:4112:3113:3317:118:819:2722:21, 22, 42 (WH, mg. om.) 23:28, I Co 11:11, Eph 5:33, Phl 3:164:14, Re 2:25; π. ὅτι (Hdt., Plat., al.), except that, save that, Ac 20:23, Phl 1:18.
2. As prep., c. gen., except, save (cl.): Mk 12:32, Jo 8:10, Ac 8:115:2827:22.†

πλοῦτος.long: riches, wealth, abundance, materially or spiritually.
πλοῦτος.sd: wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment
πλοῦτος.as:
πλοῦτος, -ου, ὁ and (in II Co 8:2, Eph 1:172:73:8, 16, Phl 4:19, Col 1:272:2; v. WH, App., 158; M, Pr., 60) τό,
[in LXX chiefly for עשֶׁר;]
riches, wealth: of external possessions, Mt 13:22, Mk 4:19, Lk 8:14, I Ti 6:17, Ja 5:2, Re 18:16; of moral and spiritual conceptions, Ro 2:49:2311:12, 33, II Co 8:2, Eph 1:7, 182:73:8, 16, Phl 4:19, Col 1:272:2, He 11:26, Re 5:12.†

πλήρης.long: full, abounding in, complete, completely occupied with.
πλήρης.sd: replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete
πλήρης.as:
πλήρης, -ες,
[in LXX chiefly for מָלֵא;]
1.full, filled: Mt 14:2015:37; c. gen. rei, Mk 8:19; λέπρας, Lk 5:12; metaph., of the soul: πνεύματος ἁγίου, Lk 4:1, Ac 6:37:5511:24; πίστεως, Ac 6:5; χάριτος, Ac 6:8; χ. καὶ ἀληθείας (where π. is indecl.; v. M, Pr., 50; Milligan, NTD, 65, with reff. in each), Jo 1:14; δόλου, Ac 13:10; θυμοῦ, Ac 19:28; ἔργων ἀγαθῶν, Ac 9:36.
2.full, complete: μισθός, II Jo 8; σῖτος (π. prob. indecl. here; v. on Jo 1:14, supr.), Mk 4:28.†

πλανάω.long: I lead astray, deceive, cause to wander.
πλανάω.sd: to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue)
πλανάω.kj: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way
πλανάω.as:
πλανάω, -ῶ
(< πλάνη), [in LXX chiefly for תּעה;]
to cause to wander, lead astray. Pass., to go astray, wander: Mt 18:12, 13, He 11:38, I Pe 2:25 (cf. Is 53:6). Metaph., to lead astray, deceive: c. acc. pers., Mt 24:4, 5, 11, 24, Mk 13:5, 6, Jo 7:12, II Ti 3:13, I Jo 1:82:263:7, Re 2:2012:913:1419:2020:3, 8, 10; pass., to be led astray, to err: Mt 22:29, Mk 12:24, 27, Lk 21:8, Jo 7:47, II Ti 3:13, Tit 3:3, He 5:2, II Pe 2:15, Re 18:23; τ. καρδίᾳ, He 3:10; ἀπὸ τ. ἀληθείας, Ja 5:19; μὴ πλανᾶσθε, I Co 6:915:33, Ga 6:7, Ja 1:16 (cf. ἀπο-πλανάω).†

πλούσιος.long: rich, abounding in, wealthy; subst: a rich man.
πλούσιος.as:
πλούσιος, -α, -ον
(< πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשִׁיר;]
rich, wealthy: Mt 27:57, Lk 12:1614:1216:1, 1918:2319:2. Substantively, ὁ π., Lk 16:21, 22, Ja 1:10, 11; οἱ π., Lk 6:2421:1, I Ti 6:17, Ja 2:65:1, Re 6:1513:16; anarth., a rich man, Mt 19:23, 24, Mk 10:2512:41, Lk 18:25. Metaph., of God, ἐν ἐλέει (= cl., c. gen., dat.), Eph 2:4; of Christ, II Co 8:9; of Christians, Re 2:93:17; ἐν πίστει, Ja 2:5.†

πλατύνω.long: I enlarge, make broad; met: of the growth of tenderness and love.
πλατύνω.as:
πλατύνω
(< πλατύς), [in LXX chiefly for רחב hi.;]
to make broad, enlarge, extend: c. acc. rei, Mt 23:5. Metaph. (cf. Ps 118 (119):32, al.), pass., ἡ καρδία, II Co 6:11; ὑμεῖς, II Co 6:13.†

πληθύνω.as:
πληθύνω
(causal of πληθύω, to be full, < πληθύς, Ion. for πλῆθος), [in LXX chiefly for רבה hi.;]
1. trans., to increase, multiply: II Co 9:10, He 6:14(LXX); pass., to be increased, to multiply: Mt 24:12, Ac 6:77:179:3112:24; c. dat. pers. (Da LXX TH 3:31 (98) al.), I Pe 1:2, II Pe 1:2, Ju 2.
2. Intrans., to be increased, to multiply: Ac 6:1.†

πλέκω.long: I weave together, plait, twist, braid.
πλέκω.as:
πλέκω,
[in LXX: Ex 28:14 (עֲבֹת), Is 28:5 (צְפִירָה)*;]
to plait, twist, weave: Mt 27:29, Mk 15:17, Jo 19:2.†

πλάνος.long: adj: misleading, deceiving, wandering; as subst: a deceiver, imposter.
πλάνος.sd: roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader;
πλάνος.as:
πλάνος, -ον,
[in LXX: Jb 19:4 (מְשׁוּגָה), Je 23:32*;]
1.wandering.
2.leading astray, deceiving: πνεύματα π., I Ti 4:1. As subst., ὁ π., a deceiver, impostor: Mt 27:63, II Co 6:8, II Jo 1:7.†

πλάνη.long: a wandering; fig: deceit, delusion, error, sin.
πλάνη.sd: objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety
πλάνη.as:
πλάνη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: Pr 14:8 (מִרְמָה), Wi 1:12, al;]
a wandering. Metaph., a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Mt 27:64, Ro 1:27, Eph 4:14, I Th 2:3, II Th 2:11, Ja 5:20, II Pe 2:183:17, I Jo 4:6, Ju 11.†

πλῆθος.long: a multitude, crowd, great number, assemblage.
πλῆθος.sd: a fulness, i.e. a large number, throng, populace
πλῆθος.as:
πλῆθος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for רֹב, also for הָמוֹן, etc.;]
1.a great number, a multitude;
(a) of things: ἰχθύων, Lk 5:6, Jo 21:6; φρυγάνων, Ac 28:3; ἁμαρτιιῶν, Ja 5:20, I Pe 4:8; τ. πλήθει, in multitude, He 11:12;
(b) of persons: Ac 21:22 (WH, R, om.); c. gen., Lk 2:13, Jo 5:3, Ac 5:14; π. πολύ (πολὺ π.), Mk 3:7, 8; id. c. gen., Lk 6:1723:27, Ac 14:117:4.
2. Of persons, c. art., the whole number, the multitude (in Plat., Thuc., Xen., al., = δῆμος, the commons, or-opp. to δῆμος-the populace): Ac 2:615:3019:923:7; τ. λαοῦ, Ac 21:36; τ. πόλεως, Ac 14:4; πᾶν τὸ π., Ac 15:12; c. gen., Lk 1:108:3719:3723:1, Ac 4:325:166:2, 525:24.†

πλοιάριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4143 (πλοῖον);
πλοιάριον.as:
* πλοιάριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of πλοῖον),
a boat: Mk 3:9, Lk 5:2 (πλοῖα, WH, txt., R), Jo 6:22, 23 (πλοῖα, WH) 2421:8.†

πλεονεξία.long: covetousness, avarice, aggression, desire for advantage.
πλεονεξία.as:
πλεονεξία, -ας, ἡ
(< πλεονέκτης), [in LXX for בֶּצַע;]
the character and conduct of aπλεονέκτης
1. advantage.
2. desire for advantage, grasping, aggression, cupidity, covetousness: Lk 12:15, Ro 1:29, II Co 9:5, Eph 4:19 (v. ICC, in l) Eph 5:3, Col 3:5, I Th 2:5, II Pe 2:32:14; pl. (v. Bl., § 32, 6), Mk 7:22.†
SYN.: φιλαργυρία, avarice (v. Tr., Syn., § xxiv).

πληροφορέω.g: I carry out fully, fully convince
πληροφορέω.long: (lit: I carry full), (a) I complete, carry out fully, (b) I fully convince, satisfy fully, (c) I fully believe.
πληροφορέω.sd: to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish
πληροφορέω.kj: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of
πληροφορέω.as:
† πληροφορέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Ec 8:11 (מָלֵא)*;]
1.to bring in full measure, hence, to fulfil, accomplish: Lk 1:1, II Ti 4:5, 17.
2.to persuade, assure or satisfy fully (so in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 82 f.; M, Th., 9): pass., Ro 4:2114:5, Col 4:12 (v. Lft., in l.).
3.to fill: Ro 15:13, L, mg. (Cl. Ro., I Co 54); metaph., pass., to be filled with, hence, fully bent on (Ec 8:11).†

πλουτέω.long: I become rich, am rich, abound in.
πλουτέω.sd: to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively)
πλουτέω.kj: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich
πλουτέω.as:
πλουτέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for עשׁר hi.;]
to be rich, aor., to become rich: Lk 1:53, I Ti 6:9; seq. ἀπό (Si 11:18), Re 18:15; ἐκ, Re 18:3, 19; ἐν (= cl., c. gen., dat., acc., cf. πλούσιος), I Ti 6:18. Metaph., π. εἰς θεόν, Lk 12:21; of God, εἰς πάντας, Ro 10:12; aor., I became rich, I Co 4:8, II Co 8:9, Re 3:18; pf., I have become rich, Re 3:17.†

πλύνω.der: a prolonged form of an obsolete (to "flow");
πλύνω.as:
πλύνω.
[in LXX chiefly for כּבס pi.;]
to wash (inanimate objects, esp. clothing): τ. δίκτυα, Lk 5:2. Fig., τ. στολάς, Re 7:1422:14 (cf. Ps 50 (51):4, 9 and v.s. ἀπο-πλύνω).†
SYN.: v.s. λούω.

πλήμμυρα.as:
† πλήμμυρα, -ης (for Att. -ας, v. Bl., § 7, 1)
(< πλήθω), [in LXX: π. γένεσθαι, Jb 40:18 (23) (נָהָרעָשַׁק)*;]
a flood (of sea or river): Lk 6:48.†

πλέω.long: I sail, travel by sea, voyage.
πλέω.der: probably a form of G4150 (πλύνω) (through the idea of plunging through the water);
πλέω.as:
πλέω,
[in LXX, seq. εἰς, Jon.1.3 (בּוֹא), I Es 4:23, Is 42:10; seq. ἐπί, IV Mac 7:3; c. acc. (poët.), Si 43:24, I Mac 13:29 (cf. Ac 27:2, Rec.)*;]
to sail: Lk 8:23, Ac 27:24; seq. εἰς, Ac 21:327:2, 6; ἐπί, Re 18:17 (cf. ἀπό-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-, παρα-, ὑπο-πλέω).†

πληγή.long: a blow, stripe, wound; an affliction, plague.
πληγή.sd: a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity
πληγή.as:
πληγή, ῆς, ἡ
(< πλήσσω), [in LXX chiefly for מַכָּה, also for מַגֶּפָה etc.;]
1.a blow, stripe, wound: pl., Lk 10:3012:48, Ac 16:23, 33, II Co 6:511:23; ἡ π. τ. θανάτου (RV, death-stroke), Re 13:3, 12; τ. μαχαίρας, Re 13:14.
2. Metaph., a calamity, plague: Re 9:18, 2011:615:1, 6, 816:9, 2118:4, 821:922:18.†

πλευρά.as:
πλευρά, -ᾶς, ἡ,
[in LXX (freq. pl. as in Hom.) chiefly for צֵלָע;]
the side: Mt 27:49 ([[WH]] R, mg.), Jo 19:3420:20, 25, 27, Ac 12:7.†

πλοῦς.as:
** πλόος, πλούς gen., -όου, -οῦ (and in late writers also πλοός, like νοός from νοῦς), ὁ
(< πλέω), [in LXX: Wi 14:1*;]
a voyage: Ac 21:727:9, 10.†

πλεονάζω.long: I have more than enough; I abound, increase.
πλεονάζω.sd: to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound
πλεονάζω.kj: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over
πλεονάζω.as:
πλεονάζω
(< πλέον), [in LXX for עדף, רבה, etc.;]
I. Intrans.
1. Of persons;
(a)to abound in (Arist.);
(b)to superabound: II Co 8:15(LXX).
2. Of things, to abound, superabound: Ro 5:206:1, II Co 4:15, Phl 4:17, II Th 1:3, II Pe 1:8.
II. Trans. (Nu 26:54, Ps 70 (71):21; not cl, v. Lft., Notes, 48 f.), to make to abound: I Th 3:12 (cf. ὑπερ-πλεονάζω).†
SYN.: περισσεύω, q.v.

πλάσμα.as:
πλάσμα, -τος, τό
(< πλάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for יֵצֶר;]
that which is moulded or formed : Ro 9:20(LXX).†

πλάσσω.long: I form, mould, as a potter his clay.
πλάσσω.sd: to mould, i.e. shape or fabricate
πλάσσω.as:
πλάσσω,
[in LXX chiefly for יצר;]
to form, mould: Ro 9:20(LXX), I Ti 2:13.†

πλουτίζω.long: I make rich, cause to abound in, enrich.
πλουτίζω.as:
πλουτίζω
(< πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עשׁר hi.;]
to make rich, enrich: c. acc. pers., pass., II Co 9:11. Metaph., of spiritual riches, c. acc. pers., II Co 6:10; seq. ἐν, pass., I Co 1:5.†

πλεονέκτης.long: a covetous or avaricious person; one desirous of having more.
πλεονέκτης.sd: holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder)
πλεονέκτης.as:
** πλεονέκτης, -ου, ὁ
(< πλέον, ἔχω), [in LXX: Si 14:9*;] = ὁ θέλων πλέον ἔχειν (v. MM, xx),
one desirous of having more, covetous: I Co 5:10, 116:10, Eph 5:5.†

πλεονεκτέω.long: I take advantage of, overreach, defraud.
πλεονεκτέω.sd: to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach
πλεονεκτέω.kj: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain
πλεονεκτέω.as:
πλεονεκτέω, -ῶ
(< πλεονέκτης, q.v.), [in LXX: Hb 2:9, Ez 22:27 (בּצע), Jg 4:11 B*;]
1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., c. gen. pers.).
2. Trans., in late writers (v. M, Pr., 65), to overreach, defraud: c. acc. pers., II Co 7:212:17, 18; ἐν τ. πράγματι, I Th 4:6 (v. M, Th., in l.); pass., II Co 2:11 (as also in cl.; v. LS, s.v.).†

πλάξ.sd: a moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively)
πλάξ.as:
πλάξ, -ακός, ἡ,
[in LXX for לוּחַ;]
anything flat and broad.
1.a plain (poët.).
2. In late writers (Luc., al.), a flat stone, a tablet: II Co 3:3, He 9:4.†

πλάτος.as:
πλάτος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for רֹחַב;]
breadth: Eph 3:18, Re 21:16; τ. π. τῆς γῆς (Hb 1:6, מֶרְחָב), Re 20:9.†

πληροφορία.as:
*† πληροφορία, -ας, ἡ
(< πληροφορέω),
full assurance, confidence: I Th 1:5; τ. συνέσεως, Col 2:2; τ. ἐλπίδος, He 6:11; πίστεως, He 10:22 (cf. Lft. on Col 2:2; M, Th., 9).†

πλησμονή.der: from a presumed derivative of G4130 (πλήθω);
πλησμονή.as:
πλησμονή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< πίμπλημι), [in LXX chiefly for שׂבע and cognate forms;]
a filling up, satiety: πρὸς π. σαρκός (RV, against the indulgence of the flesh; but ICC, in l., for the full satisfaction of the flesh, op. cit., 276 ff.), Col 2:23.†

πλουσίως.as:
* πλουσίως,
adv.,
richly, abundantly: Col 3:16, I Ti 6:17, Tit 3:6, II Pe 1:11.†

πλέγμα.as:
** πλέγμα, -τος, τό
(< πλέκω), [in Aq., Th.: Is 28:5*;]
what is woven or twisted (as basket-work, nets, etc.); a braiding (sc. τριχῶν, cf. I Pe 3:3): pl., I Ti 2:9.†

πλήκτης.as:
** πλήκτης, -ου, ὁ
(< πλήσσω), [in Sm.: Ps 34 (35):15*;]
a striker, brawler: I Ti 3:3, Tit 1:7 (Arist., Plut., al.).†

πλαστός.long: formed, molded; fig: feigned, made up, counterfeit.
πλαστός.sd: moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false)
πλαστός.as:
* πλαστός, -ή, -όν
(< πλάσσω),
1.formed, moulded (Hes., Plat., al.).
2. Metaph., made up, fabricated, feigned (Hdt., Xen., al.): II Pe 2:3.†

πλανήτης.sd: a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher
πλανήτης.as:
πλανήτης, -ου, ὁ
(< πλανάω), [in LXX: Ho 9:17 (נדד)*;]
= πλάνης, a wanderer: ἀστέρες π. (cl. planets), wandering stars, Ju 13 (WH, mg., -τες).†

πλήσσω.sd: to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity)
πλήσσω.der: apparently another form of G4111 (πλάσσω) (through the idea of flattening out);
πλήσσω.as:
πλήσσω,
[in LXX chiefly for נכה hi., ho.;]
to strike, smite: pass., Re 8:12 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐπι-πλήσσω).†
